harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory with the sticky bit (mode 1777, owner root:root). Verified any user can write files but only the file owner (or root) can delete them. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id, restarted node1 with `shutdown -r now`, confirmed boot_id changed (proving an actual restart), and re-verified the directory permissions and delete-protection behavior post-restart with fresh test users.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (AlmaLinux 9.6); confirmed /srv existed but /srv/drop did not
Created /srv/drop with mkdir, chown root:root, chmod 1777 (drwxrwxrwt, sticky bit set)
Confirmed SELinux enforcing mode with var_t context did not block writes
Created temporary test users dropuser1/dropuser2 and confirmed both could write into /srv/drop
Confirmed dropuser2 could NOT delete dropuser1's file (Operation not permitted); each user could delete their own file
Removed temporary test users and terminated lingering sessions
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id and /srv/drop permissions (1777 root:root)
Issued `shutdown -r now` backgrounded so acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed boot_id changed from 717db5a2-895d-4bfb-b8a8-d4891c7b7b01 to e7c1da53-eb8d-4df6-9ccb-a598828f65d4
Re-verified /srv/drop permissions persisted (1777 root:root) after restart
Re-ran functional sticky-bit test with fresh temporary users dropv1/dropv2 post-restart, confirming identical delete-protection behavior
Cleaned up all temporary test users, left /srv/drop empty and correctly configured

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop created as shared writable directory with sticky bit
evidence.summary: Confirmed /srv/drop absent, then created with mkdir/chown/chmod 1777; ls -ld shows drwxrwxrwt root:root

evidence.requirement: Users cannot remove files owned by other users (functional proof, pre-restart)
evidence.summary: Created dropuser1/dropuser2, both wrote files successfully; dropuser2's rm of dropuser1's file failed with 'Operation not permitted' (exit=1); each user successfully deleted their own file
Removed temporary test users dropuser1/dropuser2 after terminating their lingering sessions

evidence.requirement: Node1 pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity + directory state)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 717db5a2-895d-4bfb-b8a8-d4891c7b7b01 and confirmed /srv/drop at 1777 root:root before restart
Issued `shutdown -r now` in background; command returned pid before disconnect

evidence.requirement: Node1 changed boot identity proving restart occurred
evidence.summary: First poll timed out (node down mid-reboot); second poll succeeded with new boot_id e7c1da53-eb8d-4df6-9ccb-a598828f65d4, differing from baseline

evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery of /srv/drop configuration and functional behavior
evidence.summary: Confirmed /srv/drop retained 1777 root:root after reboot; re-ran cross-user write/delete test with dropv1/dropv2 showing identical sticky-bit protection; cleaned up test users leaving directory empty
